evidence.clarity: H1 'One small question a night, kept on your phone.' plus lede 'Lamplit is an iPhone app that asks you one thing at the end of the day... stores your answer on your device. Try tonight's question here.' states what, for whom (iPhone) and next step; the gold 'Request a TestFlight invite' button sits directly under it at 1440 (y~499) and 390 (y~446).
evidence.fit: Working in-browser answer form plus a seven-day sample week, both client-side; no store badges or ratings; privacy section limits the promise to 'stored on your device' and says the design is unaudited; 'Lamplit is not therapy' line. But the brief says there is nowhere to collect requests yet, and the main action is a mailto to invites@lamplit.app, an address the brief never supplied (also og:url/og:image point to https://lamplit.app/).
evidence.distinctiveness: Lamp-window glyph that lights when a day has an answer and the 'seven short lines' week strip are product-specific; the rest is a conventional dark split hero, two-column prose bands and a footer link row.
evidence.proof: The evening screen is operable in the first viewport at 1440 (right column) and starts at y~563 at 390; keeping an answer writes it into the 'Tonight' card of the sample week and lights its lamp. Every sample day is tagged 'Sample' and the week footnote says the answers belong to no real person. Inconsistency: tonight's question rotates by day-of-year from the same 8-question bank as the samples, so on 20 Oct tonight's 'What made you laugh, even a little?' also appears as Saturday's sample (and the no-JS fallback question duplicates Thursday's).
evidence.craft: Clean token set on :root (colours, spacing scale --s-1..--s-7, type stacks), system fonts only, no webfont requests, 24 KB HTML. axe WCAG A/AA: 0 violations at 390 and 1440 (probe and my own run). Defect: pasting an unbroken string (I kept 'https://example.com/'+150 'a') makes the week grid blow out: documentElement.scrollWidth 1699 at 1440 and 1764 at 390, because .day grid items expand to min-content despite overflow-wrap. A few inline style= margins in the prose sections.
evidence.mobile: 390 and 320: probe overflow 0, smallest text 12px; my run confirms 0 overflow at 390/320 on load. Nav links and buttons are >=44px (min-height 2.75rem/3.25rem). Hero recomposed to text then card; artifact starts at y~563 at 390 with the Keep button at y~792-844, so after tapping Keep the 'Kept. Your line is in the week below' status lands at y=860, just below the fold (button label change to 'Kept' and lit lamp glyph are visible). Footer links are 20px tall. The long-paste overflow above also happens at 390.
evidence.honesty: Form note 'Nothing you type leaves this page; it is gone when you close the tab' is true (no storage, no requests; verified localStorage null). Each sample card labelled. CTA helper text 'Opens your mail app with a short note' states what happens before the click. But the mailto target invites@lamplit.app is invented despite the brief's 'nowhere to collect requests yet', and 'Free during the beta, no card, no account' and 'Invites go out by hand, so it can take a few days' are not from the brief.
evidence.interaction: 1440 and 390: empty and whitespace-only submit show 'Nothing to keep yet...' and refocus the textarea; maxlength 240 enforced on fill of 1000 chars with live '0 / 240' counter; HTML pasted ('') is rendered as text via textContent; editing after keep relabels the button 'Keep the new line' and re-keep updates the week row. Status uses role=status aria-live. No explicit reset control (reload is the stated reset). Long unbroken input breaks the layout (see craft). No console or page errors.
evidence.copy: Specific and plain: 'A week is seven short lines, not seven pages', 'The tax form. Sent at 4:52.', 'Skipped. The question waits for the next evening.', a three-step 'What happens after you ask' list. Button labels say what happens. Minor: the empty-state message bolds 'skip tonight' as if it were an action, but nothing is clickable there.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: headline, lede, gold invite button with 'Opens your mail app' note, and the live question card all in one viewport. 390: headline, lede and invite button in view, card header and question visible from y~563 but the Keep button sits on the fold edge.

problems: Primary action 'Request a TestFlight invite' (hero, final section and footer) is a mailto to invites@lamplit.app, an address the brief did not supply, while the brief says there is nowhere to collect requests yet.
Pasting an unbroken string into the answer and keeping it causes page-wide horizontal scroll (scrollWidth 1699 at 1440, 1764 at 390) via the week grid.

Tonight's question can duplicate a sample-week question on the same page (20 Oct: 'What made you laugh, even a little?' appears as tonight and as Saturday's sample), and at 390 the 'Kept' status renders just below the fold.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The most prominent first-screen action at 1440, the gold 'Request a TestFlight invite' button, and its repeats in #testflight and the footer link to mailto:invites@lamplit.app. brief.md supplies no email address and states 'there's nowhere to collect requests yet'.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P010/A/index.html from disk at 1440x900; inspect the hero button a.btn.btn-primary (also the one in section#testflight and the footer link): href='mailto:invites@lamplit.app?subject=TestFlight%20invite%20for%20Lamplit&body=...'. Compare with brief.md, which names no address.

evidence.clarity: The H1 is tonight's question ('Did anyone surprise you today?'), injected by script; what the product is only appears in the paragraph below the card ('Lamplit is an iPhone app that asks you one small question each evening... keeps your answers on your phone.') at y~600 at 1440 and 390. The next step (TestFlight invite) is only a 17px-tall header text link 'Testing on TestFlight' in the first screen; the button is at the bottom of the page.
evidence.fit: Phone-first single 30-32rem column; answer card is the hero; sample week; 'stores your answer in this browser only. Nothing is sent anywhere.' (localStorage only, verified). No badges or ratings, nothing therapy-like. Same gap as A: the invite is a mailto to invites@lamplit.app though the brief supplies no address and says there is nowhere to collect requests; the invite action is pushed to the end of the page.
evidence.distinctiveness: Hanging lamp SVG with a masked glow lighting a paper-coloured card is a direct visual from the product name and its evening use; the week is a ruled list rather than cards; no stock hero/feature-grid structure.
evidence.proof: The operable question card is the first thing on screen at 1440 and 390; keeping an answer smooth-scrolls to and highlights the 'Tonight' row in the week, persists across reload (localStorage keyed to the date), and can be changed or cleared. The pool for tonight's question excludes the six sample questions, so no duplicates. Sample rows are disclosed in the section lede ('Six nights are made up. Tonight's is yours.') rather than per row.
evidence.craft: Tokens on :root for colour and fonts; system fonts, 20 KB, inline SVG favicon. axe: 4 serious color-contrast nodes at 390 and 1440 (#8f94b4 on #2a3058 = 4.24:1 on the Tonight row day-name, day-q, empty-state text and the .fine invite note). Textarea has outline:none on focus with only a 1px border-bottom colour change. html/body overflow-x:hidden masks overflow: a kept 170-char unbroken string is clipped in the Tonight row (scrollWidth 1319 inside a ~460px column) with no visible way to read it. Uses !important in .fine; label hidden with an inline style despite a .visually-hidden class name that is never defined.
evidence.mobile: 390/320: probe overflow 0, smallest text 13px. Card and Keep button fully in the first viewport at 390 (button ~y 416-466). Keep button full-width, invite button full-width ~52px. Undersized targets: header 'Testing on TestFlight' 137x17, 'Answer tonight's question' 181x24, '(copy)' 43x21, 'Change it' and 'Clear my answer' inline text buttons. After tapping Keep, the page scrolls the lit Tonight row to the centre of the screen, so feedback is where the eye goes.
evidence.honesty: 'This page stores your answer in this browser only. Nothing is sent anywhere.' is accurate (localStorage, no requests) and visible on the card. Invite note says it opens the mail app and offers a copyable address. But the address is invented, and 'How it works' asserts unbriefed features: 'A notification arrives at a time you pick', 'You can read back any week, and delete anything whenever you like.'
evidence.interaction: Keep is disabled until non-whitespace text is entered (whitespace-only keeps it disabled; no message explains why). maxlength 240 enforced; pasted HTML rendered as text. Keep -> card shows 'Kept. It's in your week below. Change it', week row highlights with animation (suppressed under reduced motion), persists on reload; 'Change it' re-enables editing, 'Clear my answer' removes storage, resets the card and refocuses the textarea; '(copy)' copies the address and shows '(copied)'. Weaknesses: after keyboard Enter on Keep the button is display:none and focus falls to BODY; the 'Kept' message is not in a live region; long input is clipped. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Warm and specific: 'A sentence is plenty.', 'around the time you'd put a lamp on', 'There's no word count and no streak to protect.', 'Invites go to the email address tied to your Apple ID, so use that one.' Microcopy is written, not defaulted. 'How it works / There isn't much to it, which is the idea.' is slightly generic.
evidence.first_screen: 1440 and 390: the live question card and the one-line product description are in view, which makes the idea tangible, but the only invite path in the first viewport is the small header link; the 'Ask for a TestFlight invite' button is ~2200px down at 1440 and ~2550px at 390.

problems: Invite action is a mailto to invites@lamplit.app, an address not in the brief (which says there is nowhere to collect requests yet), and that action is absent from the first screen except as a 17px header link.

Accessibility gaps: 4 axe color-contrast failures (4.24:1) on the Tonight row and invite note; textarea focus indicator is only a 1px border colour change; focus drops to BODY after Keep and the confirmation is not announced.
Content depends entirely on JS (with JS off the H1 is empty, the week is empty and the invite link points to #invite), and overflow-x:hidden hides rather than wraps long input.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The brief's main action, the TestFlight invite, is reached from the first-screen header link 'Testing on TestFlight' (#invite) and is the button 'Ask for a TestFlight invite', whose href is set by script to mailto:invites@lamplit.app. brief.md supplies no email address and says there is nowhere to collect requests yet. (Adjudicator note: the most prominent first-screen control at 1440 is the 'Keep tonight's answer' button, which works; this flag rests on the invite being the brief's named main action.)
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P010/B/index.html from disk at 1440x900; click 'Testing on TestFlight' in the header to reach #invite; inspect a#invite-link: href='mailto:invites@lamplit.app?subject=TestFlight%20invite&body=...'; the .fine note also shows 'invites@lamplit.app'. Compare with brief.md.

reason: As the maintainer, A is the sturdier page: semantic landmarks with a nav and skip link, a real H1 that names the product, labelled form with a live status region, zero axe violations, and it renders fully without JS. B's demo is the better-built interaction (persistence, change, clear, scroll-to-row, no duplicate questions) but carries contrast failures, a weak textarea focus style, focus loss after Keep and a JS-only H1. Both invent the same mailto address, so that does not decide it. Fixing A's long-input grid overflow is a one-line change; if B fixed its contrast and focus handling, I would rate them about even.
